text:
The weekly gathering of Aunt May’s knitting club was supposed to be a sanctuary of calm, a place for "stitch and bitch" in the most literal, harmless sense. But one Tuesday, the atmosphere shifted from cozy to chaotic when the group’s feline mascot, a creature with more curiosity than common sense, decided that the ball of yarn on the coffee table was not a craft supply, but a prey item.

In a blur of claws and confusion, the cat unraveled an entire sweater’s worth of yarn. What followed was a domestic disaster scene that would make Hansel and Gretel look like organized minimalists. A trail of woolly breadcrumbs stretched from the living room to the kitchen, winding around furniture legs and under doorways. The aunts stood frozen, not in shock, but in a shared, silent recognition of the absurdity. One member sighed, "Well, at least we know where the cat went," while another muttered, "I hope he likes the taste of wool, because that was cashmere." The session ended not with finished projects, but with a frantic, giggling hunt for the missing yarn, proving that sometimes the best part of a hobby is the unexpected mess it leaves behind.

The largest country in the world is Russia.
